posts.text:
What's happening now in the stock market is more than just a "correction in tech stocks."

Sure, AI CapEx concerns are legitimate and investors will always care about profitability.

But, there's more beneath the surface here.

The reality is that the market is pricing-in a major shift in the political landscape of the US.

Over the last 12 months, market expectations for a Democrat "sweep" of the US Midterm elections have tripled.

Over the last 45 days alone, these expectations are up +30 percentage points.

As it stands, markets themselves now see a near-80% chance of a Democrat "sweep" of the US Midterm elections.

President Trump has already vowed to become "Mr. Veto" if this in fact does happen.

This is post is not political, it's objective. A change in the political landscape always comes with uncertainty; markets hate uncertainty. 

Objectively, the market is in the process of pricing-in two years of political gridlock.

Could this change? Of course. But markets price-in the most probable outcome, and the odds now overwhelmingly favor the aforementioned scenario.

Tomorrow sets the stage for the next two years.

posts.text:
It's officially election day.

History says stocks are heading higher.

In fact, the S&P 500 has closed GREEN in the year following every US Midterm election since 1980.

As we noted in our analysis yesterday, we believe recent weakness in markets is largely a function of the uncertainty around Midterm elections.

However, when this uncertainty dissipates, markets react positively.

Since 1980, the S&P 500 has averaged a +14% gain in the 12 months following US Midterm elections.

Furthermore, even after divided-government outcomes, the index has averaged a +15% one-year gain, compared to +12% under single-party control.

Of course, the near-term picture will come with volatility and change.

But, if history is any guide, it's a great time to be bullish.

Turn on our post notifications at @KobeissiLetter for real-time analysis as this develops.

posts.author: WOLF
posts.text:
AMD $AMD REPORTS EARNINGS TODAY AFTER THE CLOSE, AND DATA CENTER IS NOW 58% OF ITS REVENUE

Last quarter, AMD's data center business brought in $6.7B, up +107% from a year ago.

Everything else, including PCs, gaming and embedded chips, did $4.8B, up just +8%.

Three years ago it was the other way around. In Q3 2023, data center did $1.6B and everything else did $4.2B, so data center was only about 28% of the business.

Data center first passed the rest of AMD in Q4 2024, slipped back behind for most of 2025, then retook the lead in Q4 2025 and has stayed ahead since.
